meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why did my son's essay get a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
A machine's guess. The company that sells it says not to use it alone. What else do you have?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now the essay.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing down eleven fifty-two and eleven fifty-eight. Students draft in another document and paste it in. Why is this anything more than that?

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
I've read 3.2, and I don't see that line. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. Show me what else you have.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
People change their argument between an outline and an essay. Why does that matter here? Hand it to me, I'll read the outline myself.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Five minutes after class, no warning, and nobody told me. A teenager gets put on the spot and that becomes your evidence? What exactly are you proposing, Hale?

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. Private, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing tonight. I'm agreeing to put this behind him, not because he did anything. The rest goes in my email.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday, November 12, after school. Put the date in the email tonight, along with the mark going in before December 1.
Do we have an agreement?
Yes. A private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen on Thursday, November 12, after school, whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on his record and the mark entered before December 1. I still want written confirmation that the zero is out of the gradebook and that nothing about this is on his file, along with answers to my other open points. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12 whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing on his record, and she still wants that in writing tonight plus her other points answered; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You opened the play to Act 3, Scene 2 and let her check for the quoted line herself, because it was specific, dated to his essay and something she could verify without trusting you.
What cost ground: You led with the checker score, which she dismissed as a machine guess and which cost you your opening turn before you owned the zero.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the big edits near midnight on October 28, which came close to that night and made her go shorter and harder, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she called the November 2 conversation an ambush, tell her it was the step procedure 4.1 requires, instead of moving straight to the offer.
